text:
maria: quick question — trying to profile long-running KV cache steady-state (minutes) with nsys but files balloon to 4-8GB. need to keep kernel timelines for hotspot hunting but can’t store whole-run traces. any tricks?

jon: yep. two main approaches i use: (1) narrow the capture window with nvtx markers so nsys only records the hot sections, (2) filter streams/events so we don't capture every copy/driver event. also trim traces post-capture if needed.

sam: nvtx markers are lifesaver. instrument the runner like:
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv-hot-start")
// run many batches until stable
NVTX_RANGE_POP()
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv-hot-end")
NVTX_RANGE_POP()
```
then run nsys with capture-range=nvtx so it only saves between those two markers.

maria: can you paste a sample nsys command?

jon: something like this (adapt paths/streams to your app):
```bash
nsys profile --output kv-steady --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt
  --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start "kv-hot-start"
  --capture-range-end "kv-hot-end"
  --sample=none
  --force-overwrite
  --capture-full-stack=false
  ./run_inference --config prod_workload.yaml
```
notes: --sample=none disables periodic CPU sampling to reduce size (we rely on kernel timelines). osrt is useful for the runtime markers.

leo: add: use stream filtering to exclude helper streams (prefetch/copy) if you only want compute kernels. you can do `--cuda-trace-cupti=true --cuda-trace-filter "stream:compute"` on newer nsys builds (check your version). that cuts out a lot of noise.

perf-bot: attachment: raw-trace-size report — baseline full-run 6.2GB, nvtx-windowed 48MB, stream-filtered 12MB. :bar_chart:

sam: if you can’t instrument nvtx easily, use `--capture-range=timerange` and a short warmup to compute the steady-state window offset, then capture only that slice. i usually do two runs: a short warmup run with nvtx just to find the window timestamps, then full-run with timerange.

maria: what about long-running artifacts like many small memcpy events piling up?

jon: exclude memory-trace events unless you're debugging memcpy hotpaths. you can remove api/driver tracing: `--trace=cuda,osrt` (drop nvtx if you don't need markers) or `--trace=nvtx,osrt` depending on what you want. also `--capture-child-processes=false` helps for helper daemons.

leo: post-capture trick: open the `.nsys-rep` in nsys-ui and export a filtered view (range only) or use `nsys export` to sqlite and run simple queries to extract only events of interest. smaller sqlite exports are much easier to share.

maria: any gotchas with --sample=none? worried about losing CPU-side stacks for kernel launch attribution.

jon: fair — if you need CPU stacks, use `--sample=cpu --sampling-interval=1000us` (or coarser) instead of full instrumentation. tiny sampling drastically reduces size vs full tracing. pick interval to balance fidelity.

sam: another thing — use shorter syscalls tracing: `--trace=osrt` has lower overhead than full system call tracing. and `--capture-range` + `--output=compressed` (if supported) can compress the output.

maria: awesome, thanks. i'll try nvtx-window + stream filters + coarse cpu sampling. will post sizes.

jon: also remember to set `--trace-buffer-size` larger if you do long windows, else you might miss markers. but that increases memory usage during capture.

perf-bot: quick checklist posted: 
- add NVTX markers around steady-state
- run probe to find stable window timestamps
- nsys: capture-range=nvtx or timerange
- filter streams and drop unnecessary trace types
- use coarse cpu sampling if stacks needed
- export subset via nsys-ui/sqlite for sharing

maria: perfect checklist. :thumbsup: will report back with numbers.
